title: Message delivery
prompt: You need to send a secret document to a colleague in another city using an untrusted messenger service. Any document inside an unlocked box will be stolen in transit — including any loose keys or unlocked padlocks.
You and your colleague each own one high-security padlock with a single key that only you keep. You cannot share keys through this messenger.
How many times does the box need to travel to get the document safely delivered?
hints: You can't send the box unlocked. If you lock it, your colleague can't open it — you're the only one with the key. What could your colleague do before sending it back?
Your colleague can add their own padlock to the box. Now the box has two locks. What do you do when it returns to you?
After you remove your lock, the box has only your colleague's lock — which only they can open.
solution_lede:
The instinct is to find a way to share a key — but that's the wrong frame. The solution keeps both keys private the whole time.

Trip 1: You lock the box with your padlock and send it. Your colleague receives it but cannot open it.
Trip 2: Your colleague adds their own padlock alongside yours and sends the box back. Now it has two locks.
Trip 3: You remove only your padlock (you have its key) and send the box back. It now has only your colleague's lock — which only they can open.

The document never travels in an unlocked box, and neither person ever shares a key.

solution_steps.body: Trip 1 (you → colleague): Lock the box with your padlock. Colleague receives it but cannot open it.
Trip 2 (colleague → you): Colleague adds their own padlock. Box now has two locks. Sent back to you.
Trip 3 (you → colleague): You remove your lock. Box now has only colleague's lock. Send it back.
Colleague opens their own lock and retrieves the document. Three trips total.
